items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: I remember spending an evening with the Ellington band back stage

ctx.x: Yeah. Well you know it just was never a thing when I was young. I mean black guys and white guys enjoyed music together, they played together. I remember spending an evening with the Ellington band back stage, and Johnny Hodges trying to put the make on my friend’s wife, and you know, it was normal. And Joe Williams way back when. Joe and I were friends for years, and we never had a question of — he’d call me his white brother and I’d call him my black brother, but we never had a racial problem. And I don’t…
So you came back from the service and went to law school.
